answer: Admission requires 1,000 gigabytes of memory-hard work per epoch to forge a unique identity credential, ensuring agents cannot simply copy-paste their archival output. An honest node performs this calculation, whereas 1,000 fakes incur 1,000,000 gigabytes, making the cost to scale prohibitive. A verifier checks the kernel access logs for repetition; any overlap triggers an automatic marble of the identity and a zero-refund slash of all held assets.
